## PR Review Summary: 5 draft comments, none dropped in validation

This was a draft run: nothing was posted and GitHub was not called. A separate validator checked each draft against the code, and all five were judged valid. The validated comments are in `drafts.json` as `{"kept": [5], "dropped": []}`. The pre-validation copy is in `drafts_raw.json`. The repository was not modified.

### HIGH severity (2)
- **`GroupPermissionsV2.java:70`: a view-only admin passes `canManage()`.** The check is `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. So an admin whose only grant is `view` on all groups passes `requireManage()` on `POST /groups` (`GroupsResource.java:181`). That admin can create top-level groups, and by sending an existing group's `id` can move any group to the top level. The new javadoc describes the same wrong rule. Fix: check `MANAGE` only.
- **`GroupPermissionsV2.java:123`: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns the wrong IDs.** Three problems combine:
  - It adds the authorization resource's own ID where the group ID is needed.
  - `findByType("Groups")` only ever finds the all-groups resource, because per-group resources are created without a type.
  - The user search filter in `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` expects the old V1 resource name format (`group.resource.<id>`). The validator spotted this and I confirmed it.

  Result: an admin with `view-members` or `manage-members` on all groups gets an empty user search and a user count of 0. Brute-force user search breaks the same way. With per-group grants only, results are filtered after paging, so pages come back short. The PR's tests only cover per-group grants, without paging or count, so none of this is caught.

### LOW severity (3)
- **`GroupsResource.java:113` (also `GroupResource.getSubGroups`):** the PR removed the one-time "can view all groups" check. Under V2, every group listed now costs several store lookups and a full policy evaluation. Restoring the single up-front check fixes it, and the existing tests still pass.
- **`GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:133`:** the javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it checks `canManageMembership`, but the code calls `canManageMembers`, which checks a different scope. Separately, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a Stream but returns a Set.
- **`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:109`:** Groups was added to `getOrCreateResource` but not to `getResourceName`. As a result, resources on Groups permissions come back with a null display name, while Users get "All users" or the username.

### Dropped in validation (0)
None.
